title: Separable Riemann–Zariski refinement over an arbitrary integral qcqs base
statement: Let $S$ be an integral quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme], with function field $F=k(S)$, and fix a separable closure $L/F$ [def-kun-separably-closed]. Quasi-compact quasi-separated means that $S$ has a finite affine open cover whose pairwise intersections are quasi-compact. An $L$-model is an integral scheme $T$ with a proper morphism $T\to S$ [def-weil-proper-morphism] and a factorization $\operatorname{Spec}L\to T\to S$ of the specified generic map, where $\operatorname{Spec}L\to T$ maps to the generic point. An $L$-quasi-model has instead a separated finite-type morphism $T\to S$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. All morphisms of these models are over $S$ and commute with their maps from $\operatorname{Spec}L$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Their function fields are finite separable subextensions of $L/F$. The inverse limit $RZ_L(S)$ of the underlying topological spaces of $L$-models, with the coarsest topology making their projections continuous, is quasi-compact. Its points are exactly pairs $(V,c)$ consisting of a valuation subring $V\subseteq L$ with fraction field $L$ and a morphism $c:\operatorname{Spec}V\to S$ extending the generic map. Here valuation means that $x\in V$ or $x^{-1}\in V$ for every $x\in L^\times$; no bound on its height is asserted. For every $L$-quasi-model $U$, composition induces an open injection $RZ_L(U)\hookrightarrow RZ_L(S)$, whose image consists of the pairs admitting a lift to $U$. For any finite family of $L$-quasi-models $U_i\to S$, there are an $L$-model $T\to S$ and quasi-compact open subschemes $W_i\subseteq T$ with proper dominant maps $W_i\to U_i$, compatible with the maps from $\operatorname{Spec}L$. Under the natural identification $RZ_L(T)=RZ_L(S)$, the open images $RZ_L(W_i)$ equal $RZ_L(U_i)$. If the $RZ_L(U_i)$ cover $RZ_L(S)$, the $W_i$ cover $T$. The same covering assertion applies to any selected subfamily over an open subscheme $S_0\subseteq S$: if all its $U_i$ factor through $S_0$ and its images cover $RZ_L(S_0)$, the corresponding $W_i$ cover $T\times_S S_0$.

source.place: Proposition 3.2.1, Lemma 3.2.2, Corollaries 3.2.4–3.2.5, Proposition 3.2.6 and Corollary 3.2.7, printed pp. 15–17. The relative open-cover assertion is their restriction to S_0, as used in Theorem 3.5.5, Steps 1 and 5. Primary PDF read online; local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: For any model or quasi-model $X$, take a nonempty affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}B$ over an affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $S$ with $B$ finitely generated over $A$, as in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Integrality identifies $\operatorname{Frac}A=F$ and $\operatorname{Frac}B=k(X)\subseteq L$. If $b_1,\ldots,b_n$ generate $B/A$, then $k(X)=F(b_1,\ldots,b_n)$. Each $b_j$ is algebraic separable over $F$, so adjoining them successively gives a finite separable extension. Thus all the asserted generic fields are finite separable. The same argument shows that $L$ is a separable closure of each $k(X)$.

source.place: Tag 01T1 (definition-finite-type), applied on generic affine charts; elementary field calculation.

proof.text: Every model and quasi-model is qcqs. Its structure morphism is quasi-compact by finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and is separated (proper implies separated by [def-weil-proper-morphism]), hence quasi-separated by [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated]. Since $S$ is qcqs, clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] gives both assertions about its source. No Noetherian hypothesis is used.

source.place: Tags 01KK and 01KU, lemma-separated-permanence; lemma-composition-quasi-compact. These give qcqs permanence over the given qcqs base.

proof.text: We use the following explicit construction repeatedly. If $P\to S$ is proper and has a specified $L$-point over the generic map, take the closure of its image point with the reduced induced structure of [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. It is nonempty, irreducible and reduced, hence integral [def-pc-integral-scheme]. On a chart meeting the image point its defining ideal is the kernel of the ring map to $L$, so the generic $L$-point factors through the closure and embeds its function field in $L$. The closed subscheme is proper over $S$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper], and is therefore an $L$-model. If an integral open subscheme of $P$ contains that image point densely, the induced closure restricts to that whole open, since the kernel on its affine domains is zero.

source.place: Tag 01J3, lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme, affine kernel construction; properness of the result: morphisms.tex Tag 01W5, lemma-closed-immersion-proper.

proof.text: The models form a nonempty directed partially ordered set after taking representatives: $S$ is a model; for two models take the reduced generic closure of their product, which is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition], and apply Step 3. There is at most one refinement map: the equalizer of two maps to the separated target is closed by its diagonal and [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]; its ideal vanishes generically, hence is zero on the affine domains of the integral source. Thus mutual refinements are inverse. The representatives form a set: a finite affine cover of $S$ is fixed; each finite-type source has a finite cover by finitely generated algebras over those rings (quotients by ideals in finite polynomial rings), and its gluing uses finitely many affine charts on each intersection, since it is quasi-separated by Step 2. These ring presentations, gluing maps and embeddings into the fixed set $L$ range over a set.

source.place: Tags 01W4 and 01W3, lemma-base-change-proper and lemma-composition-proper; the smallness and generic equalizer arguments are written here.

proof.text: By Step 2 and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-scheme-spectral], each model has a spectral underlying space. A refinement is proper by [lemma-nagata-proper-to-separated-target], since its source is proper over $S$ and its target separated over $S$. It is consequently quasi-compact by [def-weil-proper-morphism] and [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], so it is a spectral map. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-directed-limit-spectral] to the small directed system of Step 4. Its limit is exactly the compatible-point space with the topology in the statement. It is spectral, hence quasi-compact by [def-weil-spectral-space].

source.place: Tag 0A2Z, lemma-directed-inverse-limit-spectral-spaces; spectrality of models: properties.tex Tag 094L, lemma-quasi-compact-quasi-separated-spectral.

proof.text: For a compatible point $x=(x_X)$ form $R_x=\bigcup_X\mathcal O_{X,x_X}\subseteq L$. A refinement is dominant because it respects the specified generic points, so these are injective subring maps and the union is directed. They are local maps, hence the maximal ideals have a directed union $\mathfrak m$: it is an ideal and any element outside it has its inverse in a local ring already containing that element. Thus $R_x$ is local and dominates each $\mathcal O_{X,x_X}$. In particular the inclusion from the coordinate on the model $S$ gives $\operatorname{Spec}R_x\to S$ with the prescribed generic map as soon as $\operatorname{Frac}R_x=L$.

source.place: Local subring unions as in Tag 00IA, lemma-dominate, first paragraph of proof; the directed-union verification is written in full.

proof.text: For $f\in L^\times$, use the map $\operatorname{Spec}L\to S\times_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf P^1_{\mathbf Z}$ with projective coordinate $[1:f]$. The product is proper over $S$ by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper]; take its reduced generic closure $X_f$ by Step 3. The two standard opens of $\mathbf P^1$ cover it by [def-nagata-affine-proj], and [lemma-nagata-relative-affine-space-open-immersion] identifies their coordinates with $f$ and $f^{-1}$ on the generic point. At $x_{X_f}$ one of these coordinates is regular; hence $f$ or $f^{-1}$ belongs to $R_x$. This proves that $R_x$ is a valuation subring and that its fraction field is all of $L$.

source.place: Projective line and its two standard affine charts; graph construction corresponding to Temkin Lemma 3.2.3. The graph and local-ring calculation are written here.

proof.text: Conversely a pair $(V,c)$ lifts uniquely to every proper model by [lemma-nagata-proper-separated-valuation-extension]. The closed-point images of these lifts are compatible by uniqueness. Their local homomorphisms embed the corresponding local rings in $V$ and make $V$ dominate $R_x$. Now Step 7 says $R_x$ has fraction field $L$, so [lemma-nagata-valuation-intersection], with both fields equal to $L$, gives $V=R_x$. In the other direction the local inclusions into $R_x$ give lifts with closed-point images $x_X$; uniqueness recovers the original compatible family. Both constructions preserve the entire morphism to $S$, not just its closed-point image. This proves the asserted valuation-pair bijection even when $S$ is not separated over $\mathbf Z$.

source.place: Valuative criterion for properness; valuation domination and intersection: algebra.tex Tag 052K, lemma-x-or-x-inverse-valuation-ring. Explicit inverse constructions supplied here.

proof.text: For a quasi-model $U\to S$, [thm-nagata-compactification] and [def-nagata-compactification] give a quasi-compact open immersion into a proper $S$-scheme. Replace the latter by its reduced generic closure as in Step 3, calling it $\overline U$. This retains all of $U$ as an open subscheme. Steps 1--8 apply over the integral qcqs scheme $U$ as well. By [lemma-nagata-separated-valuation-lift-unique], composition gives an injection of valuation pairs into those on $S$. Its image equals $p_{\overline U}^{-1}(U)$: a lift to $U$ agrees with the proper lift to $\overline U$ by [lemma-nagata-proper-separated-valuation-extension]; conversely a proper lift whose closed point lands in $U$ factors through $U$, since every point of a local spectrum generalizes its closed point. Thus the image is open as a subset.

source.place: Nagata compactification of a separated finite-type morphism over a qcqs base, with generic closure; the open-image argument is written here.

proof.text: We spell out the permanence needed to compare the topologies. For any proper $U$-model $A$, its composite to $S$ is finite type by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change] and [def-weil-proper-morphism]. It is separated: its diagonal factors as $A\to A\times_U A\to A\times_S A$; the first arrow is closed and the second is a base change of the closed diagonal of $U/S$. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-comp] their composite is closed. Hence [thm-nagata-compactification] applies to $A\to S$. Taking the reduced generic closure in this compactification produces an $S$-model $\overline A$ containing $A$ openly, exactly as in Step 9.

source.place: Tag 01KU, lemma-separated-permanence (1), with its diagonal proof; finite-type composition: morphisms.tex Tag 01T3, lemma-composition-finite-type.

proof.text: For an open $O\subseteq A$ in any proper $U$-model, its inverse image in $RZ_L(U)$ corresponds, under the injection of Step 9, to $p_{\overline A}^{-1}(O)$ in $RZ_L(S)$. Indeed the proper lift over $U$, composed with $A\hookrightarrow\overline A$, is the unique proper lift over $S$ by [lemma-nagata-proper-separated-valuation-extension]. These are all the generating opens of the source topology, so the injection is open. It is also continuous: for any proper $S$-model $B$, the reduced generic closure inside $B\times_SU$ is a proper $U$-model by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper], and its map to $B$ computes the restricted centre projection. Thus inverse images of all generating opens of the target are open. This proves the homeomorphism onto the open in Step 9.

source.place: Compactification and base change as in Steps 9--10; explicit comparison of the generating opens (the open-injection clause).

proof.text: For a finite family $U_i$, form their integral compactifications $\overline U_i$ from Step 9 and take $T$ to be the reduced generic closure in $\prod_S\overline U_i$. The product is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition], so Step 3 applies. Its projections $q_i:T\to\overline U_i$ are proper by [lemma-nagata-proper-to-separated-target] and dominant because they send the specified generic point to that of $U_i$. Set $W_i=q_i^{-1}(U_i)$. Then $W_i\to U_i$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change], and dominant since $W_i$ contains the generic point of $T$. It is quasi-compact over the quasi-compact scheme $U_i$ by [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](2). In particular $W_i$ is a quasi-compact open in $T$. All morphisms commute with $\operatorname{Spec}L$ by construction. For the empty family use $T=S$.

source.place: Tags 01W4 and 01W3, proper base change and composition; product of compactifications is the common refinement construction. Quasi-compactness: schemes.tex lemma-composition-quasi-compact.

proof.text: For any model $T\to S$, proper lifting gives a bijection $RZ_L(T)\to RZ_L(S)$ by [lemma-nagata-proper-separated-valuation-extension]. It is a homeomorphism: a proper $T$-model is already a proper $S$-model by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition]; conversely the reduced generic closure in $B\times_ST$ of any $S$-model $B$ is a $T$-model by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. The respective centre projections compute both topologies. The same argument applies to the proper map $W_i\to U_i$, with their compatible generic maps from $L$, and gives $RZ_L(W_i)=RZ_L(U_i)$ as subspaces of $RZ_L(S)$: the existence and uniqueness of the proper lift to $W_i$ identifies the valuation sets, and Step 11 identifies their open embeddings. This proves exactly the open-image equality asserted for the constructed $W_i$.

source.place: Proper valuative lifting and proper composition/base change; comparison of the centre projections proves the claimed natural identifications.

proof.text: For any $y\in T$, [lemma-nagata-local-domain-valuation-dominates] supplies a valuation ring of $k(T)$ dominating $\mathcal O_{T,y}$. Extend it to a valuation ring $V$ of $L$ with [lemma-nagata-valuation-ring-extension]. The resulting local inclusion $\mathcal O_{T,y}\subseteq V$ gives a morphism $\operatorname{Spec}V\to T$ with closed point $y$. If the $RZ_L(U_i)$ cover, this pair over $S$ lifts to some $U_i$. Its composite into $\overline U_i$ and the composite through $q_i$ agree by [lemma-nagata-proper-separated-valuation-extension]. Therefore $q_i(y)\in U_i$, or $y\in W_i$, proving the covering assertion. For an arbitrary open $S_0\subseteq S$, the relative valuation subspace consists of the pairs whose morphism factors through $S_0$; equivalently their centre on $S$ is in $S_0$, so this is the open $p_S^{-1}(S_0)$ denoted $RZ_L(S_0)$. If $y\in T\times_SS_0$, the constructed valuation morphism factors through this open (its closed point does), and the selected subfamily supplies a lift to one of its $U_i$. The same uniqueness argument puts $y$ in the corresponding $W_i$. Each such $W_i$ already factors through $S_0$ via $U_i$. Hence these opens cover exactly $T\times_SS_0$, without imposing quasi-compactness on $S_0$.

source.place: Tag 00IA, lemma-dominate; extension and valuative uniqueness give the explicit pointwise covering argument, including restriction to an arbitrary open base.
